core1b.fresh_task: A mirror maker uses a wide spherical mirror to focus all parallel rays at R/2. Justify whether narrowing its aperture can improve sharpness.

stages.attempt: A mirror maker uses a wide spherical mirror to focus all parallel rays at R/2. Justify whether narrowing its aperture can improve sharpness.
stages.reconstruct: The exact normal rotates with height; reflection turns by 2α and the axis intercept depends on height. Small h/R permits sinα≈tanα≈α, giving R/2; a stop removes marginal rays and reduces spherical aberration.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved answer demonstrates this error: Treating R/2 as an exact geometrical law for wide apertures. Otherwise record insufficient evidence; compare your actual reasoning with the reconstruction.
stages.repair: Compare the ray height with radius and use the local normal construction.
stages.boundary_test: What optical trade-off accompanies narrowing aperture?
